They use body language, such as nodding and making eye contact, and respond with phrases like “I see” or “Go on”. They ask open-ended questions to encourage the speaker to talk more about their feelings and experiences. They summarise what they have heard to make sure they have understood correctly.

Active listening is a skill that can be learned and developed. It requires concentration, patience and practice. It is not always easy, especially if the speaker is expressing strong emotions or saying things we do not agree with. However, it is a vital part of building trust and maintaining healthy relationships.

Listening is not just important in personal relationships. It is also crucial in professional environments, in education and in community interactions. We often jump to conclusions before fully understanding the other person’s point of view. We might be thinking about what we want to say next, rather than truly listening. We might be checking our phones or looking at our screens instead of giving the speaker our full attention.

- Introduce the main character and their world.
